drug_class: CGRP (calcitonin gene-related peptide) antagonist / monoclonal antibody
purpose: Emgality is used to help prevent migraine headaches in adults, meaning it reduces how often you get migraines. It is also used to treat a type of severe headache called cluster headaches. By taking it regularly, many people have fewer and less severe migraine attacks.
how_it_works: Your body makes a natural chemical called CGRP, which plays a big role in causing migraine pain by widening blood vessels and triggering pain signals in the brain. Emgality is a special protein (called a monoclonal antibody) that attaches to CGRP and blocks it from doing its job. Think of it like a lock and key — Emgality locks onto CGRP so it cannot turn on the pain process that leads to a migraine.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are redness, pain, or itching at the injection site where you give yourself the shot. Some people also notice a skin reaction or mild swelling where they injected. These usually go away on their own fairly quickly.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have ever had a serious allergic reaction to any medication. Stop using Emgality and get medical help right away if you develop signs of a severe allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing, or dizziness. Let your doctor know about all medications you take and if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, since the safety in pregnancy is not fully established.
typical_dosing: For migraine prevention, you start with two injections (240 mg total) the first time, then give yourself one injection (120 mg) once a month after that. For cluster headaches, you give three injections (300 mg total) at the start of each cluster period. It comes as a pre-filled pen or syringe that you inject under the skin, usually in the belly, thigh, or upper arm.
